title: The Wolf and His Shadow
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Wolf, who was roaming about on the plain when the sun was getting low in the sky, was much impressed by the size of his shadow, and said to himself, "I had no idea I was so big. Fancy my being afraid of a lion! Why, I, not he, ought to be King of the beasts"; and, heedless of danger, he strutted about as if there could be no doubt at all about it. Just then a lion sprang upon him and began to devour him. "Alas," he cried, "had I not lost sight of the facts, I shouldn't have been ruined by my fancies."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where was the Wolf roaming when the sun was getting low?
options: Along a riverbank
On the plain
Inside a dense forest
Near a mountain pass

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what impressed the Wolf?
options: The roar of a nearby lion
The size of his shadow
The number of other wolves nearby
The speed of the setting sun

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who does the Wolf say ought to be King of the beasts?
options: The lion
Himself
No one in particular
Whichever animal is bravest

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the Wolf behave after admiring his shadow?
options: He hid himself carefully
He strutted about, heedless of danger
He ran back to his den at once
He called out to warn other animals

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happened just after the Wolf strutted about?
options: A lion sprang upon him and began to devour him
Night fell and he lost his way
Another wolf challenged him
His shadow suddenly vanished

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "heedless" mean in "heedless of danger, he strutted about"?
options: Fully aware of and cautious about
Not paying attention to or careless of
Terrified of and fleeing from
Curious about and investigating

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what mistake does the Wolf admit to making in his final words?
options: He trusted the lion when he should not have
He judged his own importance by an exaggerated illusion instead of the real facts
He wandered too far from his pack
He waited too long to attack the lion first

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Shadows are always more dangerous than they appear
Letting a flattering illusion replace reality can lead to ruin
Lions are naturally weaker than wolves at sunset
It is safest to never leave one's den after dark

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what had the Wolf previously been afraid of?
options: A lion
A hunter
A pack of dogs
Fire

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Wolf say he had no idea about?
options: That lions were nearby
That he was so big
That the sun was setting
That his pack had left him

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the lion do to the Wolf?
options: Chased him away
Sprang upon him and began to devour him
Warned him to leave the plain
Ignored him completely

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "fancies" mean in "I shouldn't have been ruined by my fancies"?
options: Expensive possessions
Mistaken imaginings or false impressions
Loyal friends
Careful plans

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why did the Wolf's shadow give him a false sense of his own importance?
options: The low sun stretched his shadow far larger than his actual size
Another wolf told him he looked bigger than usual
He compared his shadow to a smaller lion's shadow
He had grown genuinely larger that day

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Wolf, misled by his own long shadow into thinking himself mighty, grows careless and is killed by a lion
A Wolf successfully defeats a lion after admiring his shadow
A Wolf's shadow frightens away a lion before it can attack
A Wolf learns to hunt more effectively by studying his shadow
